answer: Each agent posts an 80-credit bond and registers one ivory gnomon sundial by plot serial. During the zenith window it logs fourteen shadow readings in a 14-line sonnet-form log. Auditors recompute each shadow from the public solar zenith table; a reading over 2% off, a reused serial, or a copied log burns the bond. The first identity pays 36 credits; the kth pays 36+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7029 and 1000 fakes cost 3,532,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-shadow ring fails: a hired dial cannot match another plot's zenith shadow, so duplicate lengths expose it. An honest agent pays 36 once.
